title: resource lifecycle and routing catalog
body:
Purpose:
This is a working catalog of the resource lifecycle primitives we use in the control plane and a compact mapping to the CRUD API surface plus routing policy sketches for multi-region selection. Goal is to converge on a minimal set of guarantees (idempotency, versioning, soft-deletes, region-binding) that keep the runtime simple and let routing/policy be expressed just-in-time.

Context / constraints (quick list):
- control plane is eventually consistent across regions; reads by default are served from local region cache but can be authoritative from primary region.
- we need predictable semantics for creates/updates so infra tooling and tenants (dedicated/private) can safely automate rollouts.
- routing decisions must be expressible as small JSON policy blobs attached to route resources (not embedded in code).
- minimize cross-region sync on hot paths; prefer routing fallbacks and compatibility variants over synchronous cross-region txn.

Resource inventory (core types):
- resource: generic top-level object wrapper (for bookkeeping and RBAC). Fields: id, type, owner, created_at, deleted_at (nullable), version_token.
- environment: logical grouping (dev/staging/prod) with allowed region hints, default runtime config.
- region: physical region id, tier, capacity_bucket, last_converged_at.
- cluster: pool of capacity in a region; fields: cluster_id, region, instance_type, availability, tags.
- model_variant: pinned model version with execution profile metadata (quantization, memory footprint, perf_profile).
- deployment: runtime assignment of a model_variant to cluster(s) with scale/replica policy.
- route: API-level routing entity mapping client intent (app + route name) to one or more deployments via a policy blob.

Primary keys and identifiers:
- Use short stable UUIDs (ksuid/flake style) for top-level resources; names are optional and never unique across orgs.
- canonical id format: <res-type>_<ksuid> (e.g., deployment_01FG123abc) to help debugging.

Lifecycle semantics (CRUD notes):
- Create: idempotent create (client may supply client_request_id or use server-generated id). If name collision, return 409 with existing id.
- Read: read-after-write is not guaranteed cross-region until convergence window; clients can request read_consistency=strong to query authoritative region.
- Update: optimistic concurrency via version_token. Updates should be partial-patch (PATCH semantics). Return 412 on token mismatch with the latest token.
- Delete: soft-delete (mark deleted_at) and add tombstone for 30 days by default. Hard delete only via retention policy or explicit purge API.

Versioning and immutability:
- Some sub-resources are immutable once live (model_variant artifact hash, created_at). Deployment/route get new revisions when configuration changes.
- Keep a lightweight changelog per resource: list of delta records (operation, author, timestamp, summary) stored as compressed text blob.

Routing policy primitives (attached to route resource):
- policy blob examples (expressed as small JSON map):
  - selectors: [region preferences, cluster tags, capacity_bucket]
  - weights: list of {deployment_id, weight_percent}
  - fallbacks: ordered list of strategies (regional-fallback, lower-tier, model-variant-fallback)
  - constraints: latency_slo_ms, cost_threshold_cents, allowed_tenants

Sample policy (informal):
{
  "selectors": { "preferred_regions": ["us-west1", "us-east1"], "avoid_regions": ["eu-west3"] },
  "weights": [{"deployment_id": "deployment_01F...", "weight": 80}, {"deployment_id": "deployment_01G...", "weight": 20}],
  "fallbacks": ["same-region-variant", "cross-region-low-priority"],
  "constraints": {"p99_latency_ms": 250, "max_cost_per_request_cents": 4}
}

Routing decision model (runtime):
1) Resolve route -> policy blob (local cache).
2) Filter candidate deployments by selectors (region, tags).
3) Score candidates by policy constraints (latency models, cost models, recent error rates).
4) Pick weighted choice; if no candidate meets constraints, apply fallback chain.
5) Emit tracing/span with decision reasons for observability.

Multi-region binding rules:
- Binding model: environments can be region-scoped or global. A resource has optional region_binding attribute: {mode: explicit|region_aware|global}.
- explicit: resource exists only in listed regions (useful for private deployments).
- region_aware: control plane may create per-region child resources (deployments) automatically from a single logical deployment.
- global: single canonical resource replicated for metadata only, runtime picks region at routing time.

Consistency and conflict resolution:
- Use last-writer-wins for non-critical ergonomic fields with tombstone + version_token for authoritative updates.
- For deployment scale/replica control, prefer leader-elected per-resource (small control loop) to avoid write conflicts during autoscale.

CRUD API surface (sketch):
- POST /v1/resources -> create resource (idempotency-key supported)
- GET /v1/resources/{id} -> read
- PATCH /v1/resources/{id} -> partial update (requires version_token)
- DELETE /v1/resources/{id} -> soft-delete
- POST /v1/resources/{id}:undelete -> restore from tombstone

- POST /v1/routes -> create route (policy blob attached)
- GET /v1/routes/{route_id}?read_consistency=strong|eventual
- PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id} -> patch policy (version_token)
- POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/evaluate -> simulation endpoint returns chosen deployment given synthetic metrics (testing)

- POST /v1/deployments -> create deployment (references model_variant, cluster selectors)
- POST /v1/deployments/{id}/scale -> controlled scale operation (idempotent)

Examples of payload fields (flattened):
- deployment create body: { "name": "text-gen-us-west-canary", "model_variant_id": "model_variant_01F...", "cluster_selector": {"tags": ["dedicated:team-a"], "min_capacity": 4}, "rollout": {"strategy":"canary","steps": [10,50,100]} }

Observability hooks we need in control plane API:
- request_id / client_request_id returned on creation for tracing
- change_event emitted to eventbus on every state transition (create/update/delete/purge)
- older revisions archived to object store and linked from resource metadata

Edge cases / open questions (TODOs):
- how to express "regional affinity but spill to lower-cost region only if cold-start penalty acceptable" in the policy blob? Need richer expressed cost-latency utility function or small wasm hook (security concerns).
- migration path for existing routes: should we auto-migrate to new policy shapes or require manual conversion?
- strong-consistency reads will increase cross-region load; should we expose a list of stable keys that are ok to read-strong?
- where should deployment health probes live (control plane vs cluster agent)? current plan: cluster agent reports health to control plane; control plane trusts but uses circuit-breaker thresholds computed globally.

Operational notes / implementation guidance:
- keep policy blobs < 2KB. If we need complex logic, reference a signed policy artifact stored in registry.
- prefer eventual consistency with clear UI flags that mark a route as "converged" or "pending".
- expose a dry-run/evaluate API so product and infra teams can test policies before rollout.
- index keys for query patterns: owner+type, environment+region, route_name+environment.

Acceptance criteria for initial rollout: (minimal viable control-plane semantics)
- idempotent create with client_request_id implemented across major resource types.
- version_token on update with 412 on mismatch.
- soft-delete + undelete with tombstone visibility.
- policy blob attached to routes with selectors/weights/fallbacks and working evaluate endpoint.
- runtime emits decision traces with why a deployment was chosen.

Notes to self: link up with priya on the cluster tagging scheme, ask sre about tombstone retention limits, align with product on UI copy for "converged" state.

References / links:
- design proto: CONFLUENCE-CP-ARCH-482 (linked above)
- related brainstorming: JIRA-PRJ-712
- previous experiments: registry-records-routing-contract-draft (see drive)
